:::{#exm-newton-linearized-gradient}
#### The Newton step at $x = -2.5$ as a root

At $x = -2.5$, the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) of the [cubic](algebra.qmd#def-cubic-polynomial) $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$
is $\ell(\step) = 2.25 - 5 \step$ (@exm-gradient-linear-approximation).
Setting it to $0$,

$$
\ba
0 &= 2.25 - 5 \step
&& \text{(@eq-gradient-linear-approximation-cubic)}
\\
5 \step &= 2.25
&& \text{(add } 5 \step \text{ to both sides)}
\\
\step &= 0.45,
&& \text{(divide both sides by } 5 \text{)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-newton-linearized-gradient-cubic}

so the next [iterate](#def-iterate) is $-2.5 + 0.45 = -2.05$,
the point where the [tangent line](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-tangent-line) in @fig-gradient-linear-approximation crosses $0$.
The [Newton's method](#def-newton-method) iteration $x^{(t+1)} = \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{x^{(t)} + 4 / x^{(t)}}$ of @exm-newton-method gives the same iterate.
Here $H = [-5]$ is not [positive definite](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-positive-definite),
so @thm-newton-model does not describe this step,
but @thm-newton-linearized-gradient does.

<!-- no-figure: the step is graphed in @fig-gradient-linear-approximation -->

:::
